Summary: Timetable Draft & Identity Management
Description: Create and maintain the authoritative weekly timetable draft aggregate scoped to batch/department/academic period. Satisfies FR-01, FR-02.

Summary: Create a new timetable draft
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to create a new weekly timetable draft for a given academic scope (batch, department, term), so that a governed editable timetable exists before entries and publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am an authenticated Academic Admin with TIMETABLE_CREATE permission, When I POST /api/v1/academics/timetables with timetableCode, name, academicYear, semester, departmentId, programId and effectiveFrom/To, Then a new timetables document is persisted with status=DRAFT and currentVersion="v1", And a TimetableCreated event is written to the outbox, And the response returns timetableId, status and version per the Standard Response envelope (FR-01, UC-01, sample §30).

Summary: Update draft timetable metadata
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to update the metadata of a timetable while it is still DRAFT, so that I can correct scope details before entries are finalized.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable is in status=DRAFT and I hold TIMETABLE_EDIT permission, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id} with changed metadata, Then the fields are updated with optimistic concurrency enforced, and attempting the same update on a PUBLISHED timetable is rejected with 409 (BR-05, BR-10, Exceptions §16 'Stale draft').

Summary: View timetable detail
Description: As an authorized user (Faculty, Student, Department Head, Management), I want to retrieve the full detail of a specific timetable, so that I can review its current draft or published state.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a valid timetableId and a user with TIMETABLE_VIEW permission scoped appropriately, When GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id} is called, Then the current timetable document (with its current version reference) is returned with HTTP 200 (§29).

Summary: Delete a draft timetable
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to delete a timetable that is still in DRAFT and has never been published, so that abandoned planning attempts don't clutter the catalog.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable is in status=DRAFT and has never had a published version, When I call DELETE /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}, Then it is soft-deleted, and attempting the same on a timetable with any PUBLISHED/SUPERSEDED version history is rejected with 409 (API Design §29).

Summary: Timetable Search & Views
Description: Provide indexed, filterable timetable retrieval by batch, faculty, room and department, plus export. Satisfies FR-11, UC 'View Batch/Faculty/Room Timetable'.

Summary: Search and filter timetables
Description: As an authorized user, I want to search and filter timetables by batch, faculty, room, subject, department and status with pagination, so that I can quickly find the relevant schedule.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables with filter and pagination query parameters, When the request is processed, Then results are returned within the search P95 <2sec indexed target, and only fields appropriate to my role/classification are included (FR-11, NFR §17).

Summary: View the published timetable for a batch
Description: As a Student or Faculty member, I want to retrieve the published timetable for a specific batch, so that I can see the current effective weekly schedule for my class.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch has a currently effective published timetable version, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/batch/{batchId}, Then only the effective, published schedule is returned, never a DRAFT/VALIDATING version (UC 'View Batch Timetable', API Design §29).

Summary: View the assigned timetable for a faculty member
Description: As Faculty, I want to retrieve my own assigned published timetable, so that I know my weekly teaching schedule.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am authenticated as Faculty, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/faculty/{facultyId} for my own facultyId, Then only my assigned, published entries are returned, consistent with 'VIEW assigned timetable' (RBAC §50).

Summary: View room utilization
Description: As a Facilities Manager, I want to retrieve the published schedule for a specific room, so that I can understand room utilization and plan maintenance or allocation.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a room has published timetable entries, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/room/{roomId}, Then the room's full published schedule is returned, consistent with 'View room utilization' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: View department-level timetable
Description: As a Department Head, I want to retrieve the aggregated published timetable for my department, so that I can manage departmental scheduling as a whole rather than batch by batch.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am a Department Head, When I call GET /api/v1/departments/{id}/timetable, Then all published timetables scoped to my department are returned, consistent with 'Manage department timetable' (RBAC panel 9, API Design panel 3 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Export a timetable
Description: As an authorized user, I want to export a published timetable to PDF or Excel, so that I can distribute or archive it outside the platform.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I hold TIMETABLE_EXPORT permission, When I call GET /api/v1/export for a given timetableId/scope, Then a PDF/Excel export is produced consistent with my role's field visibility, and a TimetableExported event is emitted (API Design panel 3, Events panel 10 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Timetable Entry Management
Description: Add, update and remove day/period slot assignments (Theory/Practical/Laboratory/Tutorial/Seminar/Event/Exam) within a draft timetable. Satisfies FR-02.

Summary: Add a slot entry to a draft timetable
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to add a day/period slot entry assigning a subject, faculty, room and batch, so that the weekly schedule is progressively built up.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable is in status=DRAFT, When I POST /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/entries with batchId, subjectId, facultyId, roomId, dayOfWeek, period and entryType, Then a timetable_entries document is created within the draft and a TimetableEntryAdded event is emitted (FR-02, UC 'Add Entry', sample §30).

Summary: Classify an entry by session type
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to classify each entry using the institution's defined type set (Theory, Practical, Laboratory, Tutorial, Seminar, Event, Exam), so that the conflict engine and downstream consumers can apply type-specific rules.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an entryType value is submitted, When it matches one of the configured categories (Timetable Entry Types panel 5 of the architecture diagram: TH, PR, LAB, TU, SEM, EVT, EXM), Then the entry is classified accordingly and the value is retained for search/filter and conflict-rule selection (Class Model §21).

Summary: Update a draft entry
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to update an existing slot entry while the timetable is still DRAFT, so that I can correct assignments before validation.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an entry exists in a DRAFT timetable, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/entries/{entryId} with changed fields, Then the entry is updated and a TimetableEntryUpdated event is emitted, and the same operation on a PUBLISHED timetable is rejected with 409 (BR-05, Sequence — Add/Update Entry §23).

Summary: Remove a draft entry
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to remove a slot entry from a draft timetable, so that I can correct the schedule before publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an entry exists in a DRAFT timetable, When I call DELETE /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/entries/{entryId}, Then the entry is removed and a TimetableEntryRemoved event is emitted (API Design panel 3, Events panel 10 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Support bulk entry creation from a weekly template
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to create multiple entries in bulk from a recurring weekly template, so that building a full weekly schedule doesn't require dozens of individual API calls.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a set of entries is submitted together against a DRAFT timetable, When the bulk create request is processed, Then each entry is validated individually, row-level errors are reported without aborting the whole batch, and successfully created entries are persisted, consistent with 'Support recurring schedules (weekly templates)' (Responsibilities panel 2 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Reference Validation
Description: Validate batch, subject, faculty and room references against their owning services before an entry or timetable can be published. Satisfies FR-03, BR-04, BR-09.

Summary: Validate batch, subject, faculty and room references on entry creation
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to validate batchId, subjectId, facultyId and roomId against ACD-04, ACD-03, HRM/Faculty and Facility respectively, so that no entry can ever reference an invalid or inactive resource.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an entry is submitted with batchId, subjectId, facultyId and roomId, When the service validates each reference against its owning service, Then the request succeeds only if all references exist and are active, otherwise it is rejected with 422 (Invalid subject/faculty/batch) and publication is blocked, consistent with BR-04 and Exceptions §16.

Summary: Reject cross-tenant references
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to reject any batch/subject/faculty/room reference that belongs to a different tenant, so that no timetable can ever cross tenant/institution boundaries.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a referenced resource belongs to a different tenantId than the timetable, When the reference is validated, Then the request is rejected, consistent with BR-09 'Cross-tenant references are prohibited'.

Summary: Refresh reference context on upstream reference updates
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to consume BatchUpdated and SubjectUpdated events from ACD-04 and ACD-03, so that reference validation context stays current without re-querying on every request.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a BatchUpdated or SubjectUpdated event is received for a referenced entity, When it is processed, Then the local reference-validation cache/context is refreshed and any DRAFT timetable referencing that entity is flagged for re-validation (Events Consumed §33).

Summary: Conflict Detection Engine
Description: Detect faculty, room, batch, subject-policy, calendar, availability and duplicate-entry conflicts, and persist reproducible conflict results. Satisfies FR-04, FR-10, BR-01, BR-02, BR-03, BR-06, BR-11, and the Conflict Model (§15).

Summary: Run conflict detection on a draft timetable
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to run conflict detection against a draft timetable, so that all blocking and warning-level conflicts are surfaced before I attempt publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable is in status=DRAFT with one or more entries, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/validate, Then the conflict engine checks faculty, room, batch, subject-policy, calendar, availability and duplicate-entry conflicts per the Conflict Model (§15), persists conflict_results, and the timetable transitions to VALIDATING then VALIDATED or INVALID, and a TimetableValidated event is emitted (FR-04, FR-10, UC-Validate, Sequence — Validate §24).

Summary: Detect faculty double-booking
Description: As the Conflict Engine, I want to detect when a faculty member is assigned to two overlapping slots, so that no timetable can be published with a faculty double-booking.
Acceptance Criteria: Given two entries share the same tenant+facultyId+day+period within overlapping effective scope, When conflict detection runs, Then a BLOCKING conflict of type FACULTY is recorded, consistent with BR-01 and the sample error 'Faculty FAC-100 is double-booked in MONDAY P2' (Error Contract §54).

Summary: Detect room double-booking
Description: As the Conflict Engine, I want to detect when a room is assigned to two overlapping slots, so that no timetable can be published with a room double-booking.
Acceptance Criteria: Given two entries share the same tenant+roomId+day+period within overlapping effective scope, When conflict detection runs, Then a BLOCKING conflict of type ROOM is recorded, consistent with BR-02.

Summary: Detect batch double-booking
Description: As the Conflict Engine, I want to detect when a batch/section has two overlapping classes, so that no student cohort can be scheduled into two places at once.
Acceptance Criteria: Given two entries share the same tenant+batchId+day+period within overlapping effective scope, When conflict detection runs, Then a BLOCKING conflict of type BATCH is recorded, consistent with BR-03.

Summary: Detect duplicate entries
Description: As the Conflict Engine, I want to detect duplicate entries sharing the same timetable+slot+subject/batch key, so that redundant scheduling can never silently persist.
Acceptance Criteria: Given two entries within the same timetable share an identical timetable+slot+subject/batch key, When conflict detection runs, Then a conflict of type DUPLICATE_ENTRY is recorded (Conflict Model §15).

Summary: Detect calendar and faculty/room availability conflicts
Description: As the Conflict Engine, I want to detect entries scheduled outside the academic calendar or outside faculty/room availability windows, so that publication respects institutional calendar and resource-availability policy.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an entry's date/period falls outside the published academic calendar, or outside a faculty/room's availability window, When conflict detection runs, Then a conflict of type CALENDAR or AVAILABILITY is recorded respectively, consistent with the Conflict Model (§15) and BR-07.

Summary: Revalidate on FacultyAvailabilityChanged
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to consume FacultyAvailabilityChanged events, so that any draft or operational timetable referencing that faculty member is automatically flagged for re-validation.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a FacultyAvailabilityChanged event is received for a facultyId referenced by one or more timetables, When the event is processed, Then affected draft/operational timetables are flagged and re-validation is triggered, consistent with 'Revalidate affected draft/operational timetable' (Events Consumed §33).

Summary: Retrieve conflict diagnostics for a timetable
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to retrieve the full set of conflict results for a timetable, so that I can see exactly what is blocking publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable has recorded conflict_results, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/conflicts, Then all conflicts are returned with type, severity, involved entry IDs and a human-readable message (FR-10, API Design §29).

Summary: Guarantee conflict results are reproducible
Description: As the Conflict Engine, I want conflict results to be reproducible purely from a timetable version and its reference snapshot/context, so that historical conflict diagnostics can always be independently re-derived for audit.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a historical timetable version and its reference context at the time of validation, When the conflict engine is re-run against that exact input, Then it produces the identical conflict_results set, consistent with BR-11.

Summary: Timetable Versioning & Publication
Description: Create immutable publication versions, publish only fully-validated timetables, and supersede prior effective versions. Satisfies FR-05, FR-06, FR-07, FR-08, BR-05, BR-07, BR-10, BR-12.

Summary: Publish a validated timetable
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to publish a timetable that has passed conflict validation, so that it becomes the single authoritative, effective schedule.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable is in status=VALIDATED with zero blocking conflicts, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/publish, Then a new immutable timetable_versions document is frozen and marked PUBLISHED, any prior effective version for the same scope is marked SUPERSEDED atomically, and a TimetablePublished event is emitted (FR-06, BR-05, BR-12, Sequence — Publish §25).

Summary: Block publication of an unvalidated or conflicting timetable
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to block publication unless the timetable is fully validated with zero blocking conflicts, so that no timetable with unresolved conflicts can ever become effective.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable is in status=DRAFT/INVALID or has one or more BLOCKING conflicts, When a publish action is attempted, Then it is rejected with 422 and publication is blocked, consistent with FR-06, BR-06 and the sample error contract (§54).

Summary: Enforce publication effective-from date against the academic calendar
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to validate that a timetable's effective-from date aligns with the academic calendar policy, so that a timetable can never take effect outside its governed academic period.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an effectiveFrom date is submitted for publication, When it falls outside the academic calendar policy window (per ACD-07's published calendar), Then publication is rejected with 422, consistent with FR-08 and BR-07.

Summary: Prevent mutation of published versions
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to reject any attempt to modify a published timetable_versions document, so that historical reconstruction always remains trustworthy.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable_versions document has status=PUBLISHED, When any update operation targets that document or its entries directly, Then the operation is rejected, consistent with FR-07 and BR-05 'Published versions are immutable'.

Summary: Clone the effective version into a new draft for changes
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to clone the current effective timetable version into a new draft, so that I can make mid-term changes without disturbing the currently published schedule.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable has a currently effective published version, When I initiate a change, Then a new draft version is created pre-populated with the effective version's entries, ready for edits, per the Change Workflow (§14.2).

Summary: Supersede the prior version on republication
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want the previously effective version to be automatically marked SUPERSEDED within the same transaction as a new publish, so that exactly one version is ever effective and the transition is atomic from the service's perspective.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable has a currently effective version, When a new version is published for the same scope, Then the prior version's status is atomically updated to SUPERSEDED and TimetableSuperseded/TimetableChanged events are emitted, while downstream propagation remains asynchronous (BR-08, BR-12, Sequence — Supersede §26).

Summary: Retrieve version history for a timetable
Description: As an authorized user, I want to list all versions of a timetable, so that I can review how the schedule has evolved across the term.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetableId with one or more versions, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/timetables/{id}/versions, Then all versions are returned ordered by version number with status and effective dates (API Design §29).

Summary: Reject stale writes with optimistic version locking
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to detect when a client submits an update based on a stale draft version, so that two concurrent edits can never silently overwrite each other.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a client submits an update based on a stale version reference, When the write is attempted, Then it is rejected with 409 optimistic-concurrency error, consistent with BR-10 and Exceptions §16 'Stale draft'.

Summary: Special & Ad-hoc Session Handling
Description: Govern lab-rights validation for laboratory sessions and ensure ad-hoc/special sessions never silently violate an existing published schedule. This capability is named only in the architecture diagram's Responsibilities and Key Business Rules panels ('Handle special sessions (lab, seminar, exam, events)', 'Lab sessions must be assigned faculty with lab rights', 'Ad-hoc sessions must not violate existing schedules') and is NOT elaborated with a dedicated FR/BR/UC in the ACD-05 Detailed Design Document — flagged as a scope gap requiring clarification before implementation.

Summary: Validate faculty lab rights for Laboratory entries
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to validate that a faculty member assigned to a LAB entryType holds the required lab rights/qualification, so that laboratory sessions are never scheduled with unqualified faculty.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an entry has entryType=LAB (Laboratory), When the facultyId is validated, Then the request checks a lab-rights/qualification flag on the faculty reference (source and exact field not specified in the ACD-05 DDD — needs confirmation with HRM/Faculty domain ownership) and is rejected if absent, consistent with 'Lab sessions must be assigned faculty with lab rights' (Key Business Rules panel 12 of the architecture diagram). NOTE: not specified in the DDD; the source of truth for 'lab rights' must be confirmed with architecture before implementation.

Summary: Create an ad-hoc/one-off session without disrupting the published schedule
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to create a one-off ad-hoc session (e.g. a makeup class or special event), so that exceptional scheduling needs can be accommodated without corrupting the regular published timetable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an ad-hoc session is proposed for a specific date/period, When it is validated against the currently published schedule for the same batch/faculty/room, Then it is rejected if it would violate any existing published entry, consistent with 'Ad-hoc sessions must not violate existing schedules' (Key Business Rules panel 12 of the architecture diagram). NOTE: not specified in the ACD-05 DDD as a distinct entity/workflow from a normal timetable entry — whether ad-hoc sessions get their own lifecycle/collection or reuse timetable_entries with a flag needs architectural confirmation.

Summary: Support recurring weekly templates for standard session types
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to define a recurring weekly template covering Theory, Practical, Tutorial and Seminar sessions, so that standard weekly scheduling doesn't need to be rebuilt from scratch every term.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a weekly template is defined for a batch/course combination, When a new term's draft timetable is created from that template, Then the standard recurring entries are pre-populated, consistent with 'Support recurring schedules (weekly templates)' (Responsibilities panel 2 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Event-Driven Integration
Description: Reliably publish the timetable domain event catalog via a transactional outbox and consume upstream ACD-03/04/07 and Faculty-availability events, so ACD-06, LMS, CAM, EXM and Analytics stay eventually consistent. Satisfies FR-09.

Summary: Publish domain events via transactional outbox
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want every state-changing operation to write its domain event (TimetableCreated, TimetableValidated, TimetablePublished, TimetableSuperseded, TimetableChanged, TimetableArchived, TimetableEntryAdded, TimetableEntryUpdated, TimetableEntryRemoved, TimetableConflictDetected, TimetableConflictResolved, TimetableExported) to a transactional outbox in the same transaction as the business write, so events are never lost even if the broker is temporarily unavailable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable/entry/validation/publication operation commits successfully, When the transaction completes, Then the corresponding event is durably recorded in outbox_events within the same transaction ('Timetable + Version + Conflict + Outbox', Event Architecture §31) and relayed to Kafka/RabbitMQ with retry until acknowledged.

Summary: Emit TimetablePublished to all downstream consumers
Description: As a downstream service (ACD-06, LMS, CAM, EXM, Analytics), I want to receive a TimetablePublished event with the effective timetable data, so that I can update my local projection without querying ACD-05 directly.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable version is published, When the TimetablePublished event is emitted, Then it includes eventId, entityId, correlationId, timetableVersion, effectiveFrom and status per the Event Contract schema (§34), and all listed downstream consumers can deserialize and apply it.

Summary: Consume BatchCreated, BatchUpdated and SubjectUpdated reference events
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to consume BatchCreated/BatchUpdated from ACD-04 and SubjectUpdated from ACD-03, so that batch and subject reference context stays current for validation without ACD-05 becoming a shadow master.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a BatchCreated, BatchUpdated or SubjectUpdated event is received, When it is processed, Then reference context for new/changed entities is refreshed, and any affected draft timetable's validation context is refreshed accordingly (Events Consumed §33).

Summary: Consume AcademicCalendarPublished and revalidate impacted schedules
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to consume AcademicCalendarPublished events from ACD-07, so that effective-from dates and any impacted draft/published schedules are revalidated against the updated academic calendar.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an AcademicCalendarPublished event is received, When it is processed, Then affected timetables are flagged and revalidated against the new calendar, consistent with 'Validate effective dates and impacted schedules' (Events Consumed §33).

Summary: Deduplicate inbound events using eventId
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want to deduplicate inbound events by eventId, so that redelivered or replayed events never cause duplicate side effects.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an inbound event with an eventId already processed successfully, When it is redelivered, Then the service recognizes the duplicate and skips reprocessing without error.

Summary: Route unprocessable events to a dead-letter queue
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want events that repeatedly fail processing to be routed to a dead-letter queue after retries are exhausted, so that they can be investigated and replayed without blocking the main stream.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an inbound or outbound event fails processing after the maximum configured retry attempts, When retries are exhausted, Then the event is persisted to dead_letter_events with failure context and an alert is raised, consistent with 'Downstream unavailable -> Asynchronous retry/DLQ' (Exceptions §16, Retry Strategy §56).

Summary: Idempotency, Concurrency & Transaction Integrity
Description: Guarantee safe client retries on create/entry/validate/publish commands and correct concurrent-edit handling across timetable, version and conflict writes. Satisfies BR-10, §57, §58.

Summary: Support idempotent create, entry and publish requests
Description: As an API client, I want to supply an idempotency key on create/add-entry/publish commands, so that a retried request never creates a duplicate timetable, duplicate entry or duplicate publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a request is retried with the same idempotency key and identical payload, When it is reprocessed, Then the original result is returned without re-executing the write, consistent with 'Duplicate request -> Idempotent response' (Exceptions §16, Idempotency §57).

Summary: Use MongoDB transactions for coupled timetable writes
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want timetable, version, conflict-result and outbox writes that must succeed or fail together to be wrapped in a MongoDB transaction, so that partial writes never leave the system in an inconsistent state.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a validate or publish operation touches timetables, timetable_versions, conflict_results and outbox_events, When the operation executes, Then all writes commit atomically or none do, consistent with 'Timetable + Version + Conflict + Outbox' (Event Architecture §31, Transaction Strategy §58).

Summary: Security, RBAC & Audit Governance
Description: Enforce the full role-based access matrix (including the diagram's Exam Cell and Facilities Manager roles), classify data sensitivity, and maintain an immutable audit trail. Satisfies FR-12, §49-51.

Summary: Enforce the full RBAC permission matrix
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want every endpoint to check the caller's role against the RBAC matrix (Super Admin: all permissions including GOVERN; Academic Admin: view/create/edit/validate/publish; Department Head: view/create/edit/validate within department; Registrar: view/publish-approve where workflow configured; Faculty: view assigned timetable; Student: view published timetable; Management: view/export where authorized; Service Accounts: scoped reference-read), so that only authorized actors can perform each action.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a user attempts an action without the corresponding permission for their role, When the request reaches the service, Then it is rejected with 401/403 per the HTTP Error Mapping (§55) before any business logic executes, and the full matrix in §50 is enforced consistently across every endpoint.

Summary: Grant the Exam Cell scoped permission to manage exam timetables
Description: As an Exam Cell member, I want permission to manage exam-type timetable entries where institutional policy allows, so that examination scheduling can be coordinated without requiring full Academic Admin access.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am authenticated as Exam Cell, When I create or update an entry with entryType=EXM, Then the action is permitted where policy allows, consistent with 'Manage exam timetables if applicable' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram); actions on non-exam entry types remain denied.

Summary: Grant Facilities Manager read-only access to room utilization
Description: As a Facilities Manager, I want read-only access to room schedules across the institution, so that I can plan room allocation, maintenance and utilization reporting without any ability to modify timetable data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am authenticated as Facilities Manager, When I access room timetable/utilization endpoints, Then I receive read-only results across all rooms in my scope, consistent with 'View room utilization' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Grant External API consumers scoped read-only access
Description: As an External API consumer (e.g. an ERP or LMS integration), I want read-only access limited to the scope defined for my API key, so that I can consume published timetable data without any write capability or over-broad visibility.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I authenticate as an External API client, When I call any ACD-05 endpoint, Then I receive only the data within my granted scope and read-only access, matching 'Read-only access (as per scope)' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Record an immutable, append-only history entry for every material change
Description: As a Compliance Officer, I want every draft change, validation, publication, supersession and authorization failure to be recorded as an append-only history/audit entry, so that a complete, tamper-evident audit trail always exists.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any material mutation or authorization failure occurs, When it is processed, Then a corresponding audit record is written capturing action, actorId and timestamp, and audit records can never be updated or deleted, consistent with FR-12 and the Audit Model (§48).

Summary: Classify and protect timetable data by sensitivity level
Description: As a Security Architect, I want timetable data classified into L1 Public, L2 Internal, L3 Restricted and L4 Operations-only tiers, so that access controls and exposure match each field's sensitivity.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a field is classified L3 (conflict diagnostics, actor/reason/audit) or L4 (outbox/idempotency/DLQ payloads), When a user without sufficient clearance queries timetable data, Then those fields are excluded from the response while L1 published-display fields remain visible per role (Data Classification §51).

Summary: Minimize replicated personal data
Description: As a Security Architect, I want ACD-05 to store only the minimum faculty/room/batch identifiers needed for scheduling, never authoritative personal or employment data, so that the service never becomes an unauthorized shadow copy of HRM/Faculty master data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable entry references a faculty member, When the entry is persisted, Then only the facultyId reference is stored, with no name, contact, employment or personal data replicated, consistent with 'ACD-05 minimizes replicated personal data' (Data Classification §51).

Summary: Observability, Reliability & Performance
Description: Provide structured logging, metrics, tracing, alerting and defined SLOs — including conflict-rate and stale-draft monitoring — so operations can detect, diagnose and recover from failures quickly. Satisfies §52-53, §56, §59-61.

Summary: Emit structured logs with correlation context
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want every ACD-05 request to emit a structured log with timestamp, service, tenantId, requestId, correlationId, actorId, operation and outcome, so that I can trace any request end-to-end across services.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any API call to ACD-05, When the request completes (success or failure), Then a structured log entry containing all required fields is emitted, and correlationId propagates through to any published events (Observability §52).

Summary: Expose operational metrics and distributed tracing
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want API rate/latency/errors, validation duration, conflict count, publish rate and outbox backlog exposed as metrics, plus end-to-end tracing from Gateway through ACD-05 to reference services, MongoDB, broker and consumers, so that I can monitor service health.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-05 is running in production, When metrics are scraped and traces are sampled, Then all listed metrics are available on the monitoring dashboard and a trace can be followed across the full request path (§52).

Summary: Alert on conflict-rate spikes, validation latency, publish failures and stale drafts
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want alerts configured for unexpected conflict-rate spikes, sustained validation-latency SLO breach, publish failures above threshold, growing outbox backlog, DLQ count, stale drafts above age threshold and event-consumer lag, so that incidents are caught before they impact scheduling operations.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any monitored signal crosses its defined threshold, When the breach is sustained beyond the alerting window, Then an alert fires to the on-call channel with enough context to begin triage (Monitoring and Alerts §53).

Summary: Apply bounded retry with exponential backoff for transient failures
Description: As the Timetable Management Service, I want transient failures (reference-service, broker, MongoDB timeout) to be retried with exponential backoff and jitter up to a bounded limit, so that temporary issues self-heal without manual intervention.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a transient failure occurs on a retryable operation, When the retry policy executes, Then attempts back off exponentially with jitter up to a maximum bound, and deterministic validation/conflict failures are never retried (Retry Strategy §56).

Summary: Meet indexed read/write performance targets
Description: As a Platform Architect, I want normal API calls, catalog search and validation runs to meet their defined P95 latency targets via proper indexing, so the service remains responsive at institutional scale.
Acceptance Criteria: Given production-representative load, When each workload type is exercised, Then normal API P95 <300ms, search P95 <2s and validation P95 <2s for a normal weekly timetable are met, verified in performance testing (NFR §17, Performance §61).

Summary: Validate disaster recovery via regular restore tests
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want automated MongoDB backups with tested restore procedures, so that ACD-05 can meet its defined RPO/RTO in a disaster scenario.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the configured backup schedule, When a scheduled restore test is executed against a non-production environment, Then the restored dataset is verified complete and consistent, including conflict_results reproducibility (Disaster Recovery §59).

Summary: API Standards, Error Handling & Contracts
Description: Deliver a consistent, versioned REST contract with standardized request/response envelopes and the full documented error taxonomy across all ACD-05 endpoints. Cross-cutting.

Summary: Publish and version the ACD-05 API contract
Description: As an API Consumer, I want a versioned specification covering every /api/v1/academics/timetables endpoint (create, detail, update, entries add/update/remove, validate, conflicts, publish, versions, batch/faculty/room timetable views), so that I can integrate against a stable, documented contract.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the ACD-05 service, When the API contract is published, Then it documents every endpoint in the REST API Specification (§29) with request/response schemas, and breaking changes require a new API version.

Summary: Return standardized success and error envelopes
Description: As an API Consumer, I want every response to follow the standard {success, data, meta} / {success:false, error, meta} envelope with requestId and correlationId, so that clients can handle responses uniformly.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any ACD-05 API call, When the response is returned, Then it conforms to the Request/Response JSON (§30) and Error Contract (§54) shapes.

Summary: Map every documented failure scenario to its specified HTTP status
Description: As an API Consumer, I want every failure scenario (faculty/room/batch conflict, invalid subject/faculty/batch, calendar conflict, stale draft, duplicate request, broker/downstream unavailable, unauthorized publish) mapped to its documented HTTP status, so that I can build reliable client-side error handling.
Acceptance Criteria: Given each documented failure condition occurs, When the API responds, Then it returns exactly the status defined in the HTTP Error Mapping table (§55): 400 malformed, 401 unauthenticated, 403 scope/permission denied, 404 not found, 409 version/conflict state, 422 scheduling/reference validation failure, 429 rate limited, 500 unexpected, 503 dependency unavailable.

Summary: End-to-End Scenarios & Cross-Module Integration
Description: Validate complete cross-cutting flows spanning creation, entry building, conflict resolution, publication and every listed downstream module integration (ACD-02/03/04, STM, HRM, SYS, EXM, COM, ACD-10). Satisfies Testing Strategy §69 and Cross-Module Integration panel 11.

Summary: E2E: Create Draft → Add Entries → Validate → Resolve Conflicts → Publish
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test that follows the full documented workflow (Create weekly draft, resolve references, validate calendar/effective date, run conflict engine, persist results, correct blocking conflicts, publish, mark previous version superseded, emit TimetablePublished), so that the complete authoritative-timetable lifecycle is proven to work together exactly as designed.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a fresh timetable draft is created via UC-Create Draft, When entries are added, validation is run, blocking conflicts are corrected and the timetable is republished, Then it transitions DRAFT -> VALIDATING -> VALIDATED -> PUBLISHED, and the resulting TimetableCreated/TimetableValidated/TimetablePublished events are observed, verified end-to-end (Primary Workflow §14, Testing Strategy §69).

Summary: E2E: mid-term change clones, revalidates and supersedes cleanly
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test proving the Change Workflow (clone current version into new draft, apply changes, re-run complete conflict validation, publish new effective version, retain prior version for audit, emit TimetableChanged/TimetableSuperseded) works end-to-end, so BR-08/BR-12 are continuously verified.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a timetable has a currently effective published version, When the Change Workflow (§14.2) is executed end-to-end, Then the new version becomes effective, the prior version is marked SUPERSEDED and remains queryable, and TimetableChanged/TimetableSuperseded events are observed by ACD-06/LMS/CAM/EXM/Analytics consumers.

Summary: E2E: publication blocked by an unresolved faculty conflict, then succeeds after correction
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test that creates a faculty double-booking, verifies publication is blocked, corrects the conflict, and verifies publication then succeeds, so BR-01/BR-06 are continuously verified against a realistic conflict scenario.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a draft timetable has two entries double-booking the same faculty member in the same slot, When validate is called (BLOCKING conflict recorded, publish rejected with 422) and then one entry is corrected and validate is re-run, Then the second validate returns zero blocking conflicts and the subsequent publish succeeds, verified end-to-end.

Summary: Validate integrations with ACD-02, ACD-03, ACD-04, STM, HRM, SYS, EXM, COM and ACD-10 before production sign-off
Description: As a Release Manager, I want end-to-end integration tests against every module listed in the Cross-Module Integration table executed as part of the Production Definition of Done, so that ACD-05 is not released until its downstream contracts are proven.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the ACD-05 release candidate, When the full integration suite runs against ACD-02 (semester structure), ACD-03 (subject scope), ACD-04 (batch/enrollment context), STM (faculty details & availability), HRM (facility room details & capacity), SYS (academic events & holidays), EXM (exam timetables), COM (timetable update notifications) and ACD-10 (timetable analytics), Then all contract, event-schema and E2E scenarios pass, and this gate is required before the service is marked production-ready (Production Definition of Done §70, Cross-Module Integration panel 11).
